([[Purcellville, Virginia]]) | college = *[[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] (2018–2021) *[[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] (2021–2023) | highlights = *Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2023) *Third-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2021) }} '''Jordan Tyler Miller''' (born January 23, 2000) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. He previously played for the [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]]. ==Early life and high school== Miller grew up in [[Middleburg, Virginia]] and attended [[Loudoun Valley High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.loudountimes.com/sports/loudoun-valley-grad-miller-turns-up-the-heat-in-first-season-at-miami/article_577342d0-7abe-11ec-8cdb-f300ac00b089.html|title=Loudoun Valley grad Miller turns up the heat in first season at Miami|work=[[Loudoun Times-Mirror]]|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=April 5, 2023}} He was named the Virginia High School League's Class AAAA Player of the Year as a junior after leading the team to the state championship and a 30-1 overall record. ==College career== Miller began his college career at [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]].{{cite web|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2022/03/20/3-things-you-may-not-know-miami-basketballs-jordan-miller/7031393001/|title=NCAA Tournament: 3 things you may not know about Miami basketball's Jordan Miller|first=Eric|last=Boynton|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=March 20, 2023|access-date=March 29, 2023}} He initially intended to [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his freshman season, but became a starter for the second half of the Patriots' season following a number of injuries on the team and averaged 10.4 points in 17 games played. After the season, Miller decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the coronavirus pandemic and return to Miami for a second season.{{cite web|url=https://www.loudountimes.com/sports/miller-time-at-mason-record-setting-valley-star-starting-to-shine-in-college/article_71aeabb8-3ebf-11ea-bdd5-234416566fa7.html|title=Miller time at Mason: Record-setting Valley star starting to shine in college|work=[[Loudoun Times-Mirror]]|date=January 24, 2020|access-date=March 29, 2023}} Miller averaged 12.7 points and 5.3 rebounds per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-basketball-transfer-jordan-miller-20210411-r52nmmjrfbb63gx7xtcp6rj7pa-story.html|title=Miami Hurricanes land George Mason's top scorer after losing several players|work=[[Sun Sentinel]]|date=April 12, 2021|access-date=March 29, 2023}} He averaged 15.8 points per game and was named third-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Jordan-Miller-a-key-for-the-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-now-and-the-future-183397117/|title=Jordan Miller a key for the Hurricanes now and the future|first=Christopher|last=Stock|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=February 24, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2023}} Following the end of the season, Miller entered the NCAA transfer portal. Miller ultimately transferred to [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]].{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article250591569.html|title=George Mason leading scorer Jordan Miller transfers to University of Miami|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=April 12, 2021|access-date=April 11, 2023}} He averaged 10.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists, and 1.8 steals per game in his first season with the Hurricanes.{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-miller-wong-20220412-cpxymamamfdofikf6kja2pcs2y-story.html|title=Jordan Miller to return to Hurricanes hoops team while Isaiah Wong remains undecided|work=[[Sun Sentinel]]|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2023}} Miller was named second-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] as a fifth year senior after averaging 15.3 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 1.2 steals per game in 37 starts.{{cite web|url=https://miami.rivals.com/news/men-s-bb-jordan-miller-declares-for-nba-draft-plus-other-changes|title=Men's BB: Jordan Miller declares for NBA Draft, plus other changes|first=Marcus|last=Benjamin|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} In the Hurricanes' Elite Eight game in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]] against [[2022–23 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]], he made seven of seven field goal attempts and made all 13 free throw attempts as Miami won 88–81 win.{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/basketball/a-clutch-tip-helps-jordan-miller-miami-reach-first-final-four/article_f9f40ed3-d63d-5233-8da5-261f1073e686.html|title=A 'Clutch' tip helps Jordan Miller, Miami reach first Final Four|first=Tim|last=Reynolds|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} It was the only the second "perfect game" with at least seven field goal attempts in NCAA tournament history after [[Christian Laettner]] had done so in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/jordan-miller-christian-laettner-perfect-game-hurricane-guard-achieves-texas/md34ipg5bolnybbmts6dnuh1|title=Jordan Miller matches Christian Laettner perfect game: Miami guard achieves remarkably rare feat in win over Texas|first=Kevin|last=Skiver|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=March 26, 2023|access-date=April 5, 2023}} At the end of the season, Miller declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/NBA/2023/04/05/Miami-Jordan-Miller-NBA-Draft-basketball/5301680716131/|title=Miami guard Jordan Miller
